title: Protocol for reconstitution of oligomeric assembly of NAIP5-NLRC4 inflammasome in vitro
protocol: Prepare LB media containing 30 μg/mL kanamycin.
Inoculate 5 mL of LB media in a 50 mL tube with a single colony using a sterile pipette tip.
Grow the pre-culture at 37°C for 8–12 h with shaking at 220 rpm.
Add 1 mL of the culture to 50 mL of LB media in a 250 mL conical flask.
Cultivate the culture at 37°C with continuous shaking at 220 rpm and regularly monitor OD600 of the culture.
Take the flask out of the shaking incubator and transfer it onto ice for 10 min once the culture attains an OD600 of 0.8–1.0.
Add IPTG to the chilled culture (25 μL of 1 M stock for 50 mL culture, final concentration 0.5 mM).
Return the culture flask to the incubator and enable expression to continue for 12–18 h at 25°C with shaking at 200 rpm.
Collect cultures into a 50 mL tube and centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and wash the cell pellets with 10 mL of 1× PBS.
Repeat the centrifugation step (6,000 × g for 5 min).
Remove supernatants.
Use 10 mL of protein lysis buffer to resuspend bacterial pellet (∼2 mL of lysis buffer is needed per 10 mL of expression culture).
Sonicate the bacteria on ice using Ultrasonic Homogenizer (35% intensity, 3 s pulses on/off, for 5 min) at 4°C.
Remove cell debris by centrifugation (30,000 × g, 30 min, 4°C).
Transfer clarified supernatants to a 15 mL tube.
Transfer 0.5 mL of Ni-NTA agarose beads (∼1.0 mL slurry) into a 15 mL tube.
Wash beads using 10 mL of lysis buffer three times at 4°C.
Introduce the Ni-NTA beads into the clarified lysate and incubate at 4°C for 2 h with gentle rotary agitation.
Collect the beads (4°C, 1,000 × g, 3 min) and discard the supernatant.
Wash beads with 10 mL of protein wash buffer three times.
Elute bound proteins from the beads by incubation with 0.5 mL elution buffer for 10 min at 4°C.
Repeat the elution step three times.
Collect eluates and further purify the protein by standard size-exclusion chromatography using Superdex 200 10/300 GL prepacked filtration column.
Flush the column with 1.5 column volumes of ddH2O to remove the storage solution.
Set flow rate to 0.5 mL/min.
Equilibrate the column with 1.5 column volumes of protein wash buffer at 0.5 mL/min.
Set the 1.0 mL sample loop state to "Load" in the FPLC system.
Inject protein wash buffer, whose volume is equivalent to twice of the sample loop, into the sample loop.
Repeat the injection twice.
Centrifuge the protein elute at 10,000 g and 4°C for 10 min.
Inject the protein solution into the sample loop.
Set sample loop state to "Inject" in the FPLC system.
Elute with 1 column volume of protein wash buffer and collect the fractions with the expected volume.
Run SDS-PAGE and stain gel using Coomassie blue R-250 to identify fractions that contain target protein.
Pool peak fractions containing target protein.
Use Amicon Ultra centrifugal filter unit with a 10 kDa size cutoff to concentrate pooled fractions (4°C, 5,000 × g, several 5 min spins).
Determine the protein concentration by using the BCA method.
Aliquot concentrated protein solution into PCR tubes (5 μL or 2 μg aliquot).
Snap freeze in liquid nitrogen and store the solution at -80°C.
Resuspend NAIP5-NLRC4 expressing HEK293T cell pellet in 200 μL of 1× Native lysis buffer containing 1% digitonin and fresh protease inhibitor cocktail.
Use digitonin (0.5–1.0%) in native lysis buffer or another suitable detergent such as Triton X-100, dodecylmaltoside, or Brij 96 at appropriate concentrations.
Pipette 200 μL to triturate each sample 10 times.
Repeat trituration three times over 30 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge samples at 20,000 × g for 30 min at 4°C.
Collect the clarified supernatants in fresh cold 1.5 mL tubes and discard the cell pellet.
Determine total protein concentration per sample using BCA method.
Adjust samples with 1× Native lysis buffer to equalize total protein between samples.
Maintain native lysates on ice whenever feasible until use.
Prepare a water bath at a steady temperature of 37°C in advance.
Remove one aliquot of recombinant PELO and flagellin protein from the freezer and allow it to thaw on ice.
Mix 10 μL of NAIP5-NLRC4 lysates with ATP (0.2 mM) + Mg2+ (2 mM).
Add 200 ng flagellin to the mixture.
Add 100 ng PELO to the mixture.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C water bath for 1 h.
Centrifuge samples at 4°C (20,000 × g) for 10 min.
Transfer the supernatant carefully to pre-chilled PCR tubes on ice.
Mix 1.5 μL of 2.5% Coomassie blue G-250 sample additive with 13.5 μL of the final reaction mixture from step 34 to prepare samples for Native PAGE.
Remove the white tape near the bottom of the 3%-12% NativePAGE minigel cassettes.
Carefully extract the comb to avoid any harm to the lane dividers.
Flush gel wells twice with 1× Native running buffer before loading samples.
Choose 3%–12% NativePAGE minigels for analysis of NAIP5-NLRC4 inflammasome.
Put the gels in the gel running tank.
Load 1× Native dark-blue cathode buffer into the gel wells.
Load 10 μL of prepared samples into each well.
Load 5 μL of NativeMark protein standard as marker.
Denature remaining samples with SDS sample buffer and run SDS-PAGE for control.
Fill the inner buffer chamber with ∼200 mL 1× Native dark-blue cathode buffer.
Fill the outer chamber with ∼500 mL 1× Native running buffer.
Run the gel at 150 V for 20 min.
Pause the run and carefully replace the dark-blue cathode buffer with 1× light-blue cathode buffer.
Continue the run at 150 V for another 90 min.
Disassemble the gel apparatus.
Use a metal spatula to remove the plastic casing from the gel.
Carefully trim the gel ∼1 mm below the well bottom and cut off the gel foot.
Transfer the trimmed gel to a plastic tray.
Equilibrate the gel in 10% SDS solution with shaking for 10 min.
Wash the gel with Native transfer buffer twice (1 min each).
Activate PVDF membranes with 100% methanol for 1 min.
Rinse PVDF membranes with transfer buffer.
Transfer proteins to PVDF membrane using standard wet transfer protocol.
Disassemble the gel and construct the gel “sandwich” in the transfer cassette.
Clamp tightly together to avoid air bubbles between any of the layers.
Load a cassette into the wet/tank transfer apparatus.
Transfer at 100 V for 1 hour at 4°C.
Rinse the membrane with pure methanol three times (5 minutes each) to destain the Coomassie blue G-250.
Wash the membrane with TBST buffer three times, 5 minutes each.
Incubate the PVDF membrane in TBST + 5% BSA for 1 hour at room temperature while gently shaking.
Probe the membrane with anti-HA antibody at room temperature for 3 hours to detect the monomeric and oligomeric NLRC4.
